scope: D92 private bridge admission for up to 16 bounded images under the unchanged 512 MiB accounted source-plus-destination ceiling; retain D92 failure diagnostics and lifecycle policy
initial_reservation: Full validated source DMA-BUF length plus 32 MiB unknown destination allowance, before C object, Vulkan, or AHB allocation/import. Existing classification ioctl and input validation have already completed.
settled_charge: Full source DMA-BUF length plus validated AndroidHardwareBufferProperties allocationSize; source VkMemoryRequirements alone is not the charge
charge_lifetime: Reserve slot and bytes together under mutex; shrink only after AHB size validation; retain through constructor failures, native teardown, and pending quarantine; release after native cleanup and C object free. No reaper.
thread_scope: Only accounting helpers are mutex-protected. The existing GL-owner/reference contract still serializes active create/refresh/destruction. No driver, FD, log, or wait call occurs under the accounting mutex. Concurrent helper tests do not make the active bridge API thread-safe.
limitations: 512MiB bounds charged accepted source/destination backing, not total process/GPU RAM or driver/instance/device/command/object overhead.
Sixteen image objects can increase driver overhead and direct or driver-owned FD counts; duplication/import/close ownership and fixed finite image count remain.

AHBsize is learned after allocation. An oversized rejected AHB can transiently exceed its provisional allowance before cleanup; this pre-existing post-allocation validation cannot establish an absolute transient physical-memory cap.
Unknown destination reservations may cause a safe refusal even if eventual small sizes would fit; admission never overcommits future shrink.
Pending D92 quarantine retains charges until process exit; no deferred pointer retry or reclamation is introduced.
Partial construction reservations are charged; counter snapshots across diagnostic counters remain observational.
This capacity change does not repair known asynchronous import failures or compositor poisoning after an over-limit import; graceful client-local refusal and compositor recovery remain unimplemented.

host_validation.scope: Actual patched bridge creation, budget helpers and teardown with native/GPU stand-ins plus real owned descriptors. Sixteen small imports, eight maximum backing pairs, source FD versus smaller VkMemoryRequirements, ten constructor rollback faults, teardown lock/charge probes, quarantined maximum backing refusal, independent 32-record failure cap, and mutex-ledger contention. No real GPU lifecycle, physical RAM bound, image build or runtime qualification.
host_validation.intentional_quarantine: Fixture retains LeakSanitizer roots only; it does not read, retry or reclaim bridge pointers after ownership transfer to quarantine. Retained FD and charged bytes are asserted; this is not a reclamation or leak-free claim.
host_validation.mock_staging: The pinned existing bridge fixture remains immutable; only a temporary copy receives allocation-size/fault and cleanup-boundary probes. The actual production header is applied without helper replacements.

build_scope: Offline renderer ELF and ABI build proof; installation and bounded physical presentation are separately qualified by the linked runtime reports.
runtime_scope: Two pinned 640x480 native Vulkan windows animate concurrently; a third client presents after their normal exits in the same private compositor session.
additional_runtime_scope: Three sequential private no-map resize clients on the same D93 renderer; normal healthy path only, not graceful over-limit recovery or peak-capacity measurement.
